title: Mixed Methods Research for Insights and Brand Teams
summary: Mixed methods research works only when the number and the reason meet in the data. See three designs, joint displays, and realistic timelines.
body_markdown:
What sample size does a mixed methods research study need? +


Plan 5 to 15 participants per behaviorally defined segment for the qualitative strand. The quantitative strand needs enough per segment to support statistical analysis, so sizing follows segment count, not one overall total.


How long does mixed methods research take? +


In a sequential explanatory design, a program that recruits separately for each strand often runs several weeks, because qualitative data collection cannot start until the quantitative research happens and gets analyzed. When both strands come from the same participants in the same session, findings arrive while the decision is still open.


How is mixed methods research different from running a survey plus separate interviews? +


Running both and reporting them in one deck puts quantitative and qualitative methods side by side, which is multimethod collection. Conducting mixed methods research means a survey result can be explained by a participant's own words, with a quote or clip behind it. That link exists only when the same people supply both.


What drives the cost of a mixed methods program? +


The cost of a mixed methods program is driven by segment count, incidence rate in recruitment, markets and languages in scope, and how much moderation and synthesis of the qualitative components is bought in. Running qualitative and quantitative data collection in one program removes the duplicate recruitment cost of fielding two studies.


Does an in-house mixed methods program remove the need for agency work? +


No. Agency teams remain a strong fit for complex, high-stakes quantitative and qualitative research and for design capacity a small insights function cannot staff. An in-house program covers the iterative questions that cannot wait for a commissioned cycle. Most teams run both.
